accepted.s: The average number of sitting days per year declined from approximately how many in the First Lok Sabha to approximately how many in the Seventeenth Lok Sabha (2019–24)?
accepted.x: The average sittings declined from about 135 days per year in the First Lok Sabha to about 55 days per year in the Seventeenth Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Use the paired historical figures and eliminate reversed or rounded alternatives.
accepted.sec: Sitting days - trend and comparison with early Lok Sabhas

accepted.s:
With reference to the present sitting pattern of the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. The Lok Sabha generally sits for around 60–70 days a year.
2. The UK House of Commons has more than 150 sittings a year.
3. The Lok Sabha sits for more days than the UK House of Commons.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Lok Sabha sits around 60–70 days annually, whereas the UK House of Commons has more than 150 sittings. Statement 3 reverses this comparison.
accepted.tq: Check the direction of the comparison before evaluating the statements.
accepted.sec: Sitting days - trend and comparison with early Lok Sabhas

accepted.s: Article 85(1) of the Constitution provides that:
o: The Rajya Sabha must sit for at least 100 days every year
There cannot be a gap of more than six months between two sessions of Parliament
The Lok Sabha must hold three sessions every year
Parliament must sit for at least 120 days every year
accepted.x: Article 85(1) bars a gap of more than six months between sessions but prescribes no minimum number of sitting days.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a constitutional maximum gap from a minimum sitting requirement.
accepted.sec: Sitting days - trend and comparison with early Lok Sabhas

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the usual parliamentary sessions and their periods?
o: Budget—April to July; Monsoon—September to November; Winter—January to February
Budget—February to May; Monsoon—July to August/September; Winter—November to December
Budget—January to March; Monsoon—May to June; Winter—September to October
Budget—March to June; Monsoon—August to October; Winter—December to January
accepted.x: The usual sessions are the Budget Session from February to May, the Monsoon Session from July to August/September, and the Winter Session from November to December.
accepted.tq: Match each session with its conventional time period.
accepted.sec: Sitting days - trend and comparison with early Lok Sabhas

accepted.s: During the Monsoon Session of 2026, which of the following correctly describes the productivity of the two Houses?
o: Lok Sabha 25 per cent and Rajya Sabha 16 per cent
Lok Sabha 19 per cent and Rajya Sabha 39 per cent
Lok Sabha 60 per cent and Rajya Sabha 53 per cent
Lok Sabha 39 per cent and Rajya Sabha 19 per cent
accepted.x: PRS data placed Lok Sabha productivity at 19 per cent and Rajya Sabha productivity at 39 per cent during the Monsoon Session of 2026.
accepted.tq: Read the House-wise figures without reversing the pair.
accepted.sec: Disruptions - time lost, cost, suspension of members

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Question Hour during the Monsoon Session of 2026:
1. It ran for 1 per cent of the scheduled time in the Lok Sabha.
2. It ran for 12 per cent of the scheduled time in the Rajya Sabha.
3. Sixteen questions were answered orally in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Question Hour ran for 1 per cent of scheduled time in Lok Sabha and 12 per cent in Rajya Sabha. Sixteen questions were answered orally in Rajya Sabha, not Lok Sabha; Lok Sabha had two oral answers.
accepted.tq: Separate the House-wise time figures from the House-wise number of oral answers.
accepted.sec: Disruptions - time lost, cost, suspension of members

accepted.s: How many questions were answered orally in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha respectively during the Monsoon Session of 2026?
accepted.x: Two questions were answered orally in the Lok Sabha and sixteen in the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.tq: Use the order of Houses specified in the question while reading paired data.
accepted.sec: Disruptions - time lost, cost, suspension of members

accepted.s: During the Monsoon Session of 2026, how many Bills were passed, and how many of them were debated in detail?
accepted.x: Twelve Bills were passed, but only one—the Public Examination Amendment Bill dealing with anti-paper-leak measures—was debated in detail.
accepted.tq: Retain the total and the exceptional detailed debate as a linked pair.
accepted.sec: Disruptions - time lost, cost, suspension of members

accepted.s: The estimated financial loss caused by disruptions during the Monsoon Session of 2026 was approximately:
accepted.x: The estimated loss due to disruptions during the session was ₹175 crore.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact monetary figure rather than a nearby rounded distractor.
accepted.sec: Disruptions - time lost, cost, suspension of members

accepted.s: In the Seventeenth Lok Sabha, Question Hour ran for approximately what proportion of its scheduled time?
accepted.x: During the Seventeenth Lok Sabha, Question Hour ran for only 60 per cent of its scheduled time.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the long-term Lok Sabha figure from the much lower Monsoon Session 2026 figure.
accepted.sec: Disruptions - time lost, cost, suspension of members

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding suspension-related rules in the Lok Sabha.

List-I (Rule)
a. Rule 373
b. Rule 374
c. Rule 374A

List-II (Effect)
i. Automatic suspension for five sittings or the rest of the session for grave disorder
ii. Member directed to withdraw for the day
iii. Suspension by a House motion up to the remainder of the session

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Rule 373 concerns withdrawal for the day, Rule 374 concerns suspension by House motion up to the remainder of the session, and Rule 374A provides automatic suspension for grave disorder.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure rule-effect pair and eliminate codes that reverse the suspension procedures.
accepted.sec: Disruptions - time lost, cost, suspension of members

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Rajya Sabha Rule 255 — suspension by House motion for the remainder of the session
Lok Sabha Rule 373 — withdrawal for the day ordered by the Speaker
Lok Sabha Rule 374 — suspension by House motion
Rajya Sabha Rule 256 — suspension by House motion, not beyond the remainder of the session
accepted.x: Rule 255 of the Rajya Sabha authorises the Chairman to direct withdrawal for the day. Suspension by House motion is dealt with under Rule 256.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped Rajya Sabha rule and effect.
accepted.sec: Disruptions - time lost, cost, suspension of members

accepted.s: Under Rule 255 of the Rajya Sabha, the Chairman may:
o: Refer every disorderly member to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
Automatically suspend a member for the entire session
Direct a member to withdraw for the day
Dissolve the House for grave disorder
accepted.x: Rule 255 enables the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha to direct a member to withdraw for the day.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish withdrawal from suspension.
accepted.sec: Disruptions - time lost, cost, suspension of members

accepted.s: What percentage of Bills were referred to committees in the Fourteenth, Fifteenth, Sixteenth and Seventeenth Lok Sabhas respectively?
accepted.x: The corresponding figures were 60 per cent, 71 per cent, 25 per cent and 16 per cent.
accepted.tq: Preserve the chronological order of the Lok Sabhas while reading the percentages.
accepted.sec: Bills passed without committee scrutiny

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about legislation in the Seventeenth Lok Sabha:
1. Less than one-fifth of Bills went to committees.
2. Fifty-eight per cent of Bills were passed within two weeks of introduction.
3. Thirty-five per cent of Bills were debated for less than one hour.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: less than one-fifth went to committees, 58 per cent were passed within two weeks, and 35 per cent received less than one hour of debate.
accepted.tq: When all three independently stated figures align, do not reject the comprehensive option merely because it is broad.
accepted.sec: Bills passed without committee scrutiny

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the committee scrutiny of Bills in India and the United Kingdom?
o: In India less than one-fifth of Bills go to committees, whereas in the UK every Bill is examined by committees of both Houses.
In India every Bill is examined by committees of both Houses, whereas in the UK less than one-fifth is examined.
Only the Rajya Sabha in India and only the House of Commons in the UK examine Bills through committees.
Neither country refers Bills to committees before passage.
accepted.x: Less than one-fifth of Indian Bills go to committees, while every Bill in the UK is examined by committees of both Houses.
accepted.tq: Test both sides of the comparison instead of focusing on only one country.
accepted.sec: Bills passed without committee scrutiny

accepted.s: The systematic system of Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees was introduced in India in:
accepted.x: The systematic committee system, including Department-related Standing Committees, began in 1993.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the institutional starting year from later reform proposals.
accepted.sec: Bills passed without committee scrutiny

accepted.s: Heavy reliance on ordinances and delegated legislation is associated with:
o: Declining legislative engagement and reduced parliamentary scrutiny
Increased legislative engagement and longer committee scrutiny
The abolition of the Rajya Sabha’s legislative role
The compulsory referral of every Bill to a committee
accepted.x: The increased use of ordinances under Article 123 and delegated legislation has grown as legislative engagement has fallen.
accepted.tq: Link the stated cause and effect rather than treating ordinance-making as an isolated power.
accepted.sec: Ordinance and Money Bill routes as bypass

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the proposals concerning the use of ordinances?
o: Judicial examination of urgency in light of Krishna Kumar Singh (2017)
Making every ordinance permanent without legislative approval
accepted.x: The proposals were to define immediate necessity, permit courts to test urgency, and publish reasons for ordinances. Permanent operation without legislative approval was not proposed.
accepted.tq: Identify the extreme proposal that goes beyond the stated reform measures.
accepted.sec: Ordinance and Money Bill routes as bypass

accepted.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, replaced an ordinance that had increased the sanctioned strength of judges from:
o: 38 to 42, excluding the Chief Justice of India
34 to 38, including the Chief Justice of India
accepted.x: The Bill replaced the May 2026 ordinance and increased the number of judges from 34 to 38, including the CJI.
accepted.tq: Watch both the before-and-after figures and the inclusion of the CJI.
accepted.sec: Ordinance and Money Bill routes as bypass

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026:
1. It replaced a May 2026 ordinance.
2. It was passed as a Money Bill.
3. The Rajya Sabha rejected it outright.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Bill replaced the May 2026 ordinance and was passed as a Money Bill. The Rajya Sabha only returned it; it did not reject it outright.
accepted.tq: Distinguish ‘returned’ from ‘rejected’ when testing the role of the second House.
accepted.sec: Ordinance and Money Bill routes as bypass

accepted.s: The principal constitutional concern regarding the use of the Money Bill route is that it:
o: Requires the approval of every State Legislature
Can bypass the Rajya Sabha for measures that may not strictly fall within Article 110
Can be introduced only in the Rajya Sabha
Prevents the Lok Sabha from considering financial legislation
accepted.x: The Money Bill route may bypass the Rajya Sabha for laws whose provisions may not strictly fit within Article 110. The Aadhaar Act, 2016, is cited as an example.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional consequence of the classification rather than the subject of the Bill.
accepted.sec: Ordinance and Money Bill routes as bypass

accepted.s: The NCRWC recommended minimum annual sitting days of:
o: 150 for Lok Sabha and 120 for Rajya Sabha
120 for Lok Sabha and 100 for Rajya Sabha
100 for Lok Sabha and 120 for Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution recommended 120 sitting days for Lok Sabha and 100 for Rajya Sabha.
accepted.tq: Keep the House-wise figures in their stated order.
accepted.sec: Reform proposals - NCRWC, fixed calendar, minimum sittings

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a proposal for improving parliamentary functioning?
o: Restricting all opposition debate to confidence motions alone
Making committee scrutiny mandatory before passage of Bills
accepted.x: The proposals include a fixed calendar, stronger Question Hour, mandatory committee scrutiny, and protection of opposition debate time. The proposal is to limit whips, not all opposition debate, to confidence votes and Money Bills.
accepted.tq: Separate a proposal concerning whips from the broader protection of opposition debate.
accepted.sec: Reform proposals - NCRWC, fixed calendar, minimum sittings

accepted.s: The proposed National Legislative Index is intended to provide a data-driven assessment of:
o: Only the attendance of Members of Parliament
Sittings, legislative business, disruptions, committee use and grievance redressal
The performance of State courts and tribunals
Only the financial expenditure of Parliament
accepted.x: The National Legislative Index covers sittings, business, disruptions, use of committees and grievance redressal.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that covers the complete range of functions named for the index.
accepted.sec: Reform proposals - NCRWC, fixed calendar, minimum sittings

accepted.s: A party must generally have at least what proportion of the strength of the Lok Sabha to have its leader recognised as the Leader of the Opposition?
accepted.x: The Speaker recognises the Leader of the Opposition when the party has at least one-tenth of the House’s strength, equivalent to 55 members in the Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the one-tenth recognition threshold from larger parliamentary thresholds.
accepted.sec: Role of opposition and Leader of Opposition

accepted.s: The statutory status of the Leader of the Opposition is provided under the:
o: Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977
accepted.x: The Leader of the Opposition has statutory status under the Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977.
accepted.tq: Match the office with the statute specifically dealing with its salary and allowances.
accepted.sec: Role of opposition and Leader of Opposition

accepted.s:
Which of the following are recognised tools available to the Opposition in Parliament?
1. Question Hour
2. Motions
3. Parliamentary committees
4. Appointment of the Speaker
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Question Hour, motions and committees are important opposition tools. The Opposition does not appoint the Speaker.
accepted.tq: Identify the one institutional power wrongly attributed to the Opposition.
accepted.sec: Role of opposition and Leader of Opposition

accepted.s: Since which year has the Public Accounts Committee generally been chaired by a member of the Opposition?
accepted.x: The Public Accounts Committee has been chaired by a member of the Opposition since 1967.
accepted.tq: Retain the institutional convention’s specific starting year.
accepted.sec: Role of opposition and Leader of Opposition

accepted.s: Which of the following activities is associated with PRS Legislative Research?
o: Issuing ordinances on behalf of the President
Presiding over meetings of Department-related Standing Committees
Determining the constitutional validity of Money Bills
Compiling session productivity, Bill scrutiny and reviews of State laws
accepted.x: PRS Legislative Research compiles data on session productivity, Bill scrutiny and State-law reviews. It is not a constitutional or presiding authority.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an independent legislative research organisation from formal constitutional institutions.
accepted.sec: PRS Legislative Research and Digital Sansad data

accepted.s: Official attendance and sitting data relating to Parliament is available on the Lok Sabha website through:
accepted.x: The official attendance and sitting data is available on the Lok Sabha website through Digital Sansad.
accepted.tq: Match the data source with the institution that maintains it.
accepted.sec: PRS Legislative Research and Digital Sansad data

accepted.s: The average attendance at Department-related Standing Committee meetings cited for 2026 was approximately:
accepted.x: The cited average attendance at DRSC meetings was 53 per cent.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the attendance percentage from the separate committee-referral percentages.
accepted.sec: PRS Legislative Research and Digital Sansad data

accepted.s: According to the PRS Annual Review of State Laws 2025, State Assemblies met on average for approximately:
accepted.x: State Assemblies met for an average of 24 days in 2025.
accepted.tq: Use the exact average rather than the higher individual figure for Odisha.
accepted.sec: State legislatures - productivity, AP sittings

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the contrasting sitting days of Odisha and Nagaland Assemblies in 2025?
accepted.x: Odisha Assembly met for 43 days, while Nagaland Assembly met for only 7 days.
accepted.tq: Read the state-wise figures as a direct contrast and avoid reversing them.
accepted.sec: State legislatures - productivity, AP sittings

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding State Legislatures:
1. Many Assemblies met only to satisfy the constitutional requirement relating to the six-month gap.
2. More than 600 Bills were passed by State Assemblies during the period reviewed.
3. About 33 per cent of the Bills were passed in a single sitting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Many Assemblies met merely to comply with the six-month requirement; more than 600 Bills were passed, and about 33 per cent were passed in a single sitting.
accepted.tq: Check each institutional trend independently before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: State legislatures - productivity, AP sittings

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 123 — ordinance-making power of the Governor
Article 174 — six-month interval between sessions of a State Legislature
Article 178 — Deputy Speaker of a State Legislative Assembly
Article 178 — office of the Deputy Speaker in a State Assembly
accepted.x: Article 123 concerns the President’s ordinance-making power. The Governor’s ordinance-making power is under Article 213; Article 174 and Article 178 are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Detect the constitutional Article swap involving ordinance-making authority.
accepted.sec: State legislatures - productivity, AP sittings

accepted.s: In how many States was the office of Deputy Speaker vacant, and for how long was it vacant in Jharkhand according to the cited review?
accepted.x: The Deputy Speaker’s office was vacant in eight States, and it had remained vacant in Jharkhand for 21 years.
accepted.tq: Keep the number of States and the duration of the vacancy as separate data points.
accepted.sec: State legislatures - productivity, AP sittings

accepted.s: The Budget Session of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly in 2026 was held from:
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Budget Session 2026 ran from 11 February to 7 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Check both the opening and closing dates rather than relying on the month alone.
accepted.sec: State legislatures - productivity, AP sittings

accepted.s: In the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly, the agenda for the Budget Session 2026 was fixed by the Business Advisory Committee chaired by:
accepted.x: The Business Advisory Committee fixing the agenda was chaired by Speaker Chintakayala Ayyanna Patrudu.
accepted.tq: Apply the authority test: identify who presides over the relevant legislative committee.
accepted.sec: State legislatures - productivity, AP sittings
